progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: The mitosis video: chromosome, set, homologous pair, diploid, haploid, chromatid, sister chromatids, centromere, the counting rule, interphase and S phase, the four steps of mitosis, the model cell and the human 46, 92, 92, 46 tracker. The first video of this series: a gamete carries one set, alleles are versions of a gene, sexual reproduction gives new combinations. The DNA copying video: DNA is copied accurately before division. Not assumed: meiosis, prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, the second division, crossing over, non-sister chromatids, independent assortment, 2 to the power n.
progression.startsWith: Two brothers with the same parents who look different, and the question of how a cell halves its chromosome number and makes gametes that differ from each other.
progression.stopsAfter: Saying why gametes must be haploid; saying meiosis is one copying and two divisions making four haploid cells; saying what happens in prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I and meiosis II; tracking chromosome and chromatid numbers; saying why crossing over and assortment make new combinations but not new alleles; counting whole-chromosome combinations as 2 to the power n; saying how fertilisation restores the number; contrasting mitosis and meiosis on the same model; applying the counts and stage recognition to an unseen case. No Punnett squares, no genotype ratios, no non-disjunction.
progression.nextLesson: DNA in prokaryotes and eukaryotes: how DNA is arranged in different kinds of cell. The later variation video returns to crossing over, assortment, random fertilisation and mutation together.

teaching.task: Explain how meiosis halves a cell's chromosome number and makes gametes that differ from each other.
teaching.causalExplanation: If gametes were made by mitosis each would carry two sets and the number would double every generation, so a cell copies its DNA once and divides twice. In prophase I homologous partners pair gene against gene and non-sister chromatids swap matching pieces, which makes new combinations of existing alleles. In metaphase I the pairs line up and each pair faces either way by chance, in anaphase I the homologous partners separate with their centromeres intact, which halves the number of sets, and in meiosis II the sister chromatids separate. Fertilisation then joins two haploid gametes and restores the number.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Starts from two different brothers, shows the doubling problem with a crossed chain, reuses the model cell with alleles marked, runs each stage with the same stage strip as mitosis, tracks the numbers on the same tracker, counts combinations with coins and a doubling grid, and compares the two divisions on the model cell.
teaching.openingDecision: Two brothers have the same parents and each began from one sperm and one egg carrying one set of chromosomes. How does a cell halve its chromosome number and make gametes that differ from each other?
teaching.understandingCheck: For a pea plant body cell with 14 chromosomes in 7 pairs and no crossing over, give the chromosomes in each gamete, the number of combinations and the chromosomes in a fertilised egg, and name the division and stage and the chromosome count per cell for a drawn cell with six lined-up chromosomes in three pairs.
teaching.curriculumScope: Model meiosis, crossing over and independent assortment and explain chromosome continuity (Module 5). Sub-stage names inside prophase I, chiasma, linkage, non-disjunction, spermatogenesis and oogenesis detail and genotype prediction are held back.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the b05a model cell with long and short chromosome bars, centromere discs, allele beads with dotted same-gene links, spindle fibres, stage strip with meiosis I and II dividers, count tracker, combinations grid and compare board. Colour key: plum is one parent's set and teal the other's, cream centromere discs with ink outline, alleles as white beads with a letter, amber for tags and emphasis, grey for crossed wrong ideas.
design.transitionPlan: The family scene draws gametes into zygotes; the doubling chain is crossed and the board wipes to the correct chain; the b05a model cell returns and gains allele beads; the stage strip lands with a meiosis I divider; a camera push reaches the paired chromosomes for crossing over; the board stays for metaphase I and the ghost line-up appears beside it; the second-division chips land with a divider and the left cell enlarges; the four-cell row builds under the parent; the tracker draws on and shrinks; the compare board builds beside the full tracker; the attempt board removes tracker and strip and they return in the feedback; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.holdPurpose: Hold on the two brothers and the question

scenes.visualReference: Body cell with a 46 ticker, a mitosis arrow making a sperm and an egg tagged 46, a zygote climbing to 92 and 184 with a grey cross, then the correct chain 46, 23, 46
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the cause for halving before meiosis is named: gametes made by mitosis would double the number every generation

scenes.visualReference: The b05a model cell (long and short plum and teal bars) with labelled allele beads and dotted same-gene links

scenes.visualReference: Four bars doubling into joined threads with alleles on both chromatids, the stage strip with a meiosis I divider, and homologous partners sliding side by side
scenes.teachingReason: Starts the first division and gives the reason for pairing: one partner of each pair can then go to each end

scenes.visualReference: Paired long chromosomes enlarged, inner chromatids lit, an amber break mark between the two genes, and a CrossOver swap of the lower pieces
scenes.teachingReason: Shows what crossing over is before naming it, and separates non-sister from sister chromatids
scenes.narrationCue: break at the same place and swap the matching pieces / non-sister chromatids / This is crossing over
scenes.motionPurpose: A push reaches the pair, the two inner chromatids light, both break at the same level and the lower pieces swap with their colours following their origin
scenes.onScreenChange: The camera pushes to the pair; scribble circles land on the inner plum and teal chromatids in turn; an amber break mark appears between the two genes on both; the lower pieces swap over three seconds; "non-sister chromatids" and "crossing over" write on

scenes.visualReference: The same board with the four long chromatids tagged A B, A b, a B, a b, a crossed ghost bead labelled new and a caption
scenes.teachingReason: Shows crossing over makes new combinations of existing alleles and no new alleles
scenes.narrationCue: It does not make new alleles / new combinations of the alleles already there / even the sister chromatids

scenes.visualReference: The nuclear envelope dashing away, spindle poles and fibres, and the two pairs sliding to the middle with one partner facing each pole
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the first lining-up and how it differs from mitosis (pairs, not single chromosomes)
scenes.narrationCue: the nuclear envelope breaks down / metaphase one / one partner facing each end

scenes.visualReference: Same board with coin flips above each pair, a TwoWays shuffle landing on line-up 1 and a ghost board showing line-up 2
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the direction is chance for each pair and names independent assortment after the idea
scenes.narrationCue: Which partner faces which end is chance / plum long and teal short on the left / This is independent assortment
scenes.motionPurpose: A coin flips above each pair in turn and the pairs face either way, a ghost board shows the other line-up, and the name writes on
scenes.onScreenChange: A coin flips above each pair one at a time and each pair slides to face either way, landing on line-up 1; a ghost copy appears beside it with the short pair flipped and tagged "line-up 2"; "independent assortment" writes on in amber
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold both line-ups side by side

scenes.visualReference: Line-up 1 whole X shapes travelling to opposite poles with discs staying whole, brackets for one of each kind, and two cells with half the number
scenes.teachingReason: Shows what separates in the first division and that this is the step that halves the number
scenes.narrationCue: the fibres pull the homologous partners apart / the centromeres do not split / one of each kind of chromosome, which is one set / half the chromosome number

scenes.visualReference: Meiosis II divider and stage chips, a grey tag for no copying between divisions, the left cell enlarged with its chromosomes lining up on their own and chromatids separating
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the cause for a second division and shows what separates in it
scenes.narrationCue: A gamete cannot keep doubled chromosomes / In anaphase two, the centromeres split / the two cells get different chromosomes

scenes.visualReference: FourCells row under the parent cell with letter labels and haploid tags, a bracket for four different cells and a crossing-over toggle that collapses them to two kinds twice
